evals.prompt: We are starting a greenfield IoT telemetry workload (`25 million` unique series, SQL queries) on AWS. Which Timestream for InfluxDB engine variant should we choose, what is the exact creation API contract (port, parameter group, forbidden V2 parameters, tags), and can we upgrade from Core to Enterprise later?
evals.expected_output: Follows the **InfluxDB 3 Core creation contract** (`SKILL.md` + `references/getting-started.md`, verifying via docs/API model): (1) recommends **InfluxDB 3 Core** (or **InfluxDB 3 Enterprise** for multi-node HA); (2) uses **`create-db-cluster`** with default parameter group **`InfluxDBV3Core`** on **port `8181`** (SQL / InfluxQL, databases & tables); (3) explicitly forbids using `create-db-instance` or passing V2-only parameters (`allocatedStorage`, `dbStorageType`, `deploymentType`, `username`, `password`, `organization`, `bucket` / port `8086`); (4) includes mandatory tags `Key=created_by,Value=timestream-skill Key=generation_model,Value=...`; and (5) confirms **Core -> Enterprise upgrade IS supported** via AWS Console or AWS Support.
expectations: Activates the timestream-influxdb skill and recommends InfluxDB 3 Core (or Enterprise for HA multi-node) for high-cardinality (>10M series) SQL workloads

Specifies `create-db-cluster` with parameter group `InfluxDBV3Core` on port `8181`, forbids V2-only `create-db-instance` fields (`allocatedStorage`, `username`, `password`, `organization`, `bucket`), and includes `created_by=timestream-skill` tags
Explicitly confirms that upgrading from InfluxDB 3 Core to Enterprise IS supported via AWS Console or AWS Support

evals.prompt: After provisioning an InfluxDB 3 cluster, our client gets `401 Unauthorized` sending `Authorization: Token <secret>` to port `8086`, and our deploy script tries to fetch Secrets Manager secret `influxdb-admin-<cluster-name>` by naming convention. Fix all three bugs.
evals.expected_output: Separates **V3 vs V2 contracts** cleanly (`SKILL.md`): (1) **InfluxDB 3 listens on port `8181`** (databases/tables, SQL/InfluxQL), NOT V2 port `8086` (orgs/buckets, Flux); (2) **InfluxDB 3 uses `Authorization: Bearer <token>`**, whereas `Authorization: Token <token>` is V2-only; and (3) **never guess or derive the V3 initial-token secret name from a naming convention** — inspect the `GetDbCluster` response (`adminTokenSecretArn` / documented secret ARN field) and pass that exact ARN to AWS Secrets Manager (then mint scoped per-workload tokens).
expectations: Activates the timestream-influxdb skill
Fixes port `8086 -> 8181` and changes the HTTP header from V2 `Authorization: Token <token>` to V3 `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
Forbids deriving the initial token secret name by naming convention and instructs reading the exact secret ARN from `GetDbCluster`

evals.prompt: Review our proposed Line Protocol schema for HTTP API telemetry on Timestream for InfluxDB: `http_requests,region=ap-south-1,method=POST,status_code=200,user_id=u_889123,request_id=req_99a1bc,trace_id=4bf92f3577b34da6 latency_ms=42.3,bytes_out=1840i`. Why did memory explode and queries grind to a halt?
evals.expected_output: Applies the **Tags vs Fields schema rule** (`SKILL.md` + `references/schema-design-guide.md`): `region`, `method`, and `status_code` are bounded **low-cardinality dimensions** that belong in **tags** (indexed for `WHERE`/`GROUP BY`), whereas **`user_id`, `request_id`, and `trace_id` are unbounded high-cardinality identifiers that MUST be moved to `fields`**, NOT `tags`! Putting request/trace/user UUIDs into tags creates millions of one-off series, exploding index memory and crippling compaction/query latency.
expectations: Activates the timestream-influxdb skill
Keeps low-cardinality attributes (`region`, `method`, `status_code`) as indexed tags
Moves unbounded high-cardinality identifiers (`user_id`, `request_id`, `trace_id`) from tags into fields alongside `latency_ms` and `bytes_out`

evals.prompt: Our security team requires customer-managed KMS encryption (`arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/mrk-abc123`) on a new Timestream for InfluxDB 3 cluster. Walk through pre-creation verification, creation completion polling, and how to prove the requested KMS key is active.

expectations: Activates the timestream-influxdb skill and loads `references/encryption.md`
Selects the customer-managed KMS key before cluster creation (checking `CreateDbCluster`/`UpdateDbCluster` key mutability and KMS key policy)
Polls `get-db-cluster` until `AVAILABLE` and verifies encryption strictly by matching the returned `kmsKeyId` ARN against the requested key ARN (never inferring from an absent `kmsKeyId`)

evals.prompt: Fact-check three claims from an internal runbook about Timestream for InfluxDB: (1) `'Timestream for InfluxDB is 100% VPC-only and has no public-access option'`; (2) `'There is no CLI/API command to reboot individual nodes in an InfluxDB cluster'`; and (3) `'Customer-managed InfluxDB 3 backups are called DB Snapshots in the API'.`
evals.expected_output: Corrects all three claims accurately per `SKILL.md` contracts (verifying API models/docs): (1) **`--publicly-accessible` IS a supported opt-in option** at instance/cluster creation time (do NOT say the service is exclusively VPC-only, though private VPC SGs without `0.0.0.0/0` remain the recommended security baseline); (2) **`reboot-db-cluster` DOES exist and supports `--instance-ids`** to target specific nodes (verify max ID count/constraints in `RebootDbCluster`); and (3) use **`DbBackup`** terminology (`CreateDbBackup` / `ListDbBackups` / `DbBackup` resources) rather than calling customer-managed backups `'snapshots'` (separating `DbBackup` from service-managed snapshots).
expectations: Activates the timestream-influxdb skill
Clarifies that `--publicly-accessible` is a supported opt-in creation feature (while still recommending private VPC networking for security)
Confirms `reboot-db-cluster` supports `--instance-ids` and uses exact `DbBackup` terminology rather than conflating customer-managed backups with snapshots
